learning_objective: 🎯 Learn the step-by-step journey of how a corporate giant is born—from a simple idea in a promoter's mind to a fully legal Joint Stock Company!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: It all starts with an idea! A 'Promoter' conceives the idea for a business, checks if it is practically and financially feasible, arranges resources, and prepares the necessary documents to form the company.

This is the legal registration of the company. The promoter submits documents (MoA, AoA) to the Registrar of Companies (RoC). If satisfied, the RoC issues a 'Certificate of Incorporation'. The company is legally born on this date!

It is the constitution or the most important document of the company. It defines the company's name, registered office, main objectives, liability of members, and authorized capital. A company cannot do anything outside its MoA.
This document contains the internal rules and regulations for managing the company's day-to-day affairs (like rules for issuing shares or conducting meetings).

fun_activity.title: 🏗️ Be the Promoter!
fun_activity.instructions: You want to start 'Mars Tourism Private Limited'. First, you get the idea (Promotion). Then you name it and write the rules (MoA & AoA). Then you register it (Incorporation). Finally, you ask the public for money (Capital Subscription - only for public companies!). You just formed a company!

exam_tips: 📌 A Private Company can start business immediately after getting the Certificate of Incorporation, but a Public Company must also undergo the 'Capital Subscription' stage.
📌 MoA defines the relationship between the company and outsiders. AoA defines the internal relationship between the company and its members.
📌 'Minimum Subscription' is 90% of the issued amount. If a public company doesn't receive this within 120 days, it must return the money to applicants.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Promoter is neither an agent nor a trustee of the company, but stands in a fiduciary (trust) capacity.
⭐ The Certificate of Incorporation is conclusive evidence of the regular formation of the company.
⭐ A Prospectus is an invitation to the general public to buy the shares or debentures of a public company.
